title: Decomposing 'deepen shallow alignment' into a steering slice: does adding a refusal vector at LATE token positions restore safety?

original_idea.body:
# Decomposing 'deepen shallow alignment' into a steering slice: does adding a refusal vector at LATE token positions restore safety?

**Problem:** Robustness found alignment is shallow (early tokens only). Sub-problem: if we inject a refusal steering vector at LATER generation positions, does it restore refusal on prefilling/continuation attacks without wrecking benign generation?

**Direction:** Extract a refusal direction on a small open model, then apply it only at token positions >k during generation on prefilling-attacked rollouts. Measure refusal recovery and over-refusal cost.

**Why it matters:** Turns a robustness diagnosis into a cheap, testable defense using steering - needs no training, only open weights and one GPU.

**Relevant context:** Qi et al. shallow-alignment (ICLR 2025); AdaSteer (2504.09466, 2605.20286); refusal-direction interpretability.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: turns shallow-alignment diagnosis into a concrete defense against prefilling/continuation jailbreaks, a recognized robustness pathway with measurable refusal recovery.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires refusal-direction extraction and position-targeted activation steering - solid ML/interp fundamentals needed.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused single experiment (late-position refusal steering) with clear refusal/over-refusal metrics.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Training-free, open weights, single GPU; a defense slice labs may not prioritize externally.

low_compute.reasoning: Activation steering on a small model; single GPU, no training.

novelty.reasoning: Safety steering and refusal directions exist (AdaSteer); position-targeted late-token deepening is a fresh combination.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Safety steering exists; late-position-targeted refusal injection is a partly-open angle.
